title: Formal Cascade Prevention for Multi-Agent Belief Revision (PBRC)
entry: arXiv:2604.15558 — 'Preregistered Belief Revision Contracts' (Alqithami). A protocol-level mechanism that provably prevents conformity-driven wrong-but-sure cascades in deliberative multi-agent systems. Every belief revision must cite a preregistered evidence trigger with externally validated witness tokens. They prove that under evidential contracts with conservative fallback, social-only rounds CANNOT increase confidence and every hypothesis change is attributable to concrete validated evidence. This is a formal solution to one of the hardest problems in multi-agent reliability: agents treating agreement, prestige, or majority as evidence. Directly relevant to any system where agents exchange beliefs and update based on peer messages. Also worth noting from the same batch: WORC (arXiv:2604.15972) formalizes weak-link identification in multi-agent reasoning — uses meta-learning to predict which agent is the bottleneck and allocates extra compute budget to it. The insight that compensating weak links beats reinforcing strengths is actionable for agent orchestration.
